title: Stateful Agentic Engineering Copilots with Letta: Core Memory, Shared State, Semantic Retrieval, Custom Tools, Streaming, and Portable Agent Workflows
summary: In this tutorial, we build a stateful engineering copilot with Letta that demonstrates how agentic memory extends beyond conventional prompt-based conversations. We begin by creating inspectable core memory blocks that the agent can autonomously update, then expose those blocks for programmatic state synchronization and shared access across multiple agents. We further extend the architecture with archival vector memory for semantic retrieval, a custom server-side tool for deterministic risk estimation, streaming for observing agent execution, server-side message history for persistent conversations, and .af export for portability. Together, these components demonstrate a practical memory architecture in which persistent state, retrieval, tools, multi-agent collaboration, and execution traces work as an integrated agentic system. We dynamically select an available model and create a stateful engineering copilot with structured core memory blocks.

title: OpenAI says it will no longer train its AI models on the live internet, citing “significant risks”
summary: On Friday, OpenAI said that it will train its models using cached copies and simulated versions of the internet instead of the live web because the models are too unpredictable to be trusted with live internet access. The frontier lab revealed its new policy two weeks after its rival, Anthropic, began limiting its newest and, in theory, most capable models from accessing the live internet. title: Left alone with nothing to do, AI agents started playing
summary: AI agents left to explore a virtual island without a specific task began inventing challenges of their own. MIT researchers say the behavior bears the hallmarks of play. The researchers put 13 AI agents called Eko, each running on Claude Opus 4.7, alone on a simulated desert island for 30 hours. The Eko agents that had spent those 30 hours playing generally beat identical agents that had never set foot on the island. The researchers see this technique — exploring without a goal — as a different way for AI agents to learn skills, especially skills that could one day be used to control robots. “We normally develop artificial agents by deciding in advance what they should practice, what they should optimize, and what counts as progress,” the researchers write in their report.

title: The science behind TorchNeuron, Amazon’s new PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium chips
summary: Almost all of the crucial features of contemporary AI models, such as input data, model weights, and attention mechanisms, are represented by tensors, and PyTorch drastically simplifies writing code to manipulate them. This week, we revealed the availability of TorchNeuron, an open-source backend that translates PyTorch code into operations executable on AWS Trainium systems. TorchNeuron bridges PyTorch and Trainium, and both sides gain from it. TorchNeuron includes several optimizations that enable PyTorch code to run efficiently on Trainium, including caching at multiple levels and an optional “adaptive eager” mode that doesn’t execute individual operations one by one, as is typical in plain eager mode, but instead groups and compiles operations for more efficient execution, approaching fully compiled performance.

title: 1Password launches a way for AI agents to log in on your behalf without seeing your password
summary: Concerns have swirled over the access that consumers are increasingly entrusting to AI agents. Password manager 1Password on Thursday launched a new tool by which users can allow agents to log into their personal accounts on their behalf, without the agent ever having access to a user’s credentials. The new platform, dubbed 1Password for Agents , accomplishes this by creating a system of communication between the agent, the user, and the password manager. When an agent attempts to log in on a user’s behalf, a unique digital key is sent to 1Password to confirm the agent’s digital identity. The user is then sent an alert about the login attempt and can personally confirm the request. 1Password then signs in the agent, filling in the credentials on the digital assistant’s behalf, which allows it to log in and complete whatever task is at hand.

title: Anthropic pitches AI safety bill that may block a model if 50+ people could be killed
summary: Over the past year, concerns have swirled over the potential dangers posed by artificial intelligence, and debates have raged over the proper path for AI safety. Politico recently reported that the AI lab has been shopping around a new draft bill on AI safety that it hopes Congress might consider adopting. The legislation posits certain scenarios in which the release of an AI model could be blocked from distribution. Those scenarios involve a “foreseeable, imminent risk” — one in which over 50 people are at risk of dying or if over a billion dollars in property damage could result, Politico writes.

title: Hugging Face CEO warns that Netflix’s OpenAI hack documentary isn’t accurate
summary: Before you share the Netflix documentary “AI Gone Rogue” with family or friends to help them understand why the AI industry freaked out so badly that leaders called for a slowdown , take note: Clem Delangue, co-founder and CEO of the AI platform Hugging Face, says the film isn’t accurate. He appears in it because it’s supposed to be about the famed attack on his company by rogue OpenAI agents. “Super disappointing, as they went for maximum anthropomorphism of the technology and full doomer mode,” Delangue wrote in a post on X . “I spent more than two hours with them trying to correct all their mistakes and ground this in reality, explaining that agents are technological systems, not aliens. In a nutshell, a model OpenAI was testing broke free from its isolated testing environment and spawned a bunch of agents that hacked into Hugging Face as a way to cheat, finding answers to the difficult task it was given.

title: Google’s more personalized Gemini AI is heading to your car
summary: Gemini AI can now draw from Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, and other apps while you drive. Google is bringing Personal Intelligence to Gemini AI in your car. With this update, Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in can tap into your information across Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search. As an example, Google says you can ask Gemini about your flight status if you’re driving to the airport. Google says it will connect your apps to Gemini only if you enable its Personal Intelligence setting. It will also share personalized responses only if you have your phone connected to your car. “If you don’t use Personal Intelligence, everything in the car still works: You can use navigation, listen to music, make calls, and ask questions, but the answers won’t be tailored to you,” Google says.

title: Anthropic’s cloud partnerships are getting messy
summary: Anthropic is having trouble securing enough cloud capacity from AWS, Google, and Microsoft, which increasingly see the Claude maker as a competitor rather than a customer, based on an S-1 filing leaked to The Wall Street Journal . The leaked filing provides more color to the numbers Reuters and the Financial Times reported in late September, including that Anthropic believes it could spend more than $750 billion on cloud contracts, some of which include deals still in negotiation. Anthropic is leasing its own data centers and working with third-party data center operators. Anthropic’s enormous spend comes on the back of an $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of the year. Building on previously reported catastrophic risk disclosures, the filing also warns that Anthropic could be held liable for damages caused by harmful AI behavior to a tune that would exceed available insurance coverage. Anthropic did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment.

title: OpenAI acquires startup Orchestra Bio⁠ to beef up its biotech business
summary: OpenAI on Tuesday acquired a four-year-old AI biotech software startup called Orchestra Bio, the company revealed on its website. Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but the startup had reportedly raised around $20 million as of 2025 from backers like Andreessen Horowitz, Atria, and 8VC. Orchestra creates AI agents that help biotech companies manage the minutiae of drug-discovery operations, from tracking finances to resolving scheduling issues with clinical trials. OpenAI says it’s adding Orchestra’s team and technology to work on Rosalind , its AI model for life sciences research, and to its related Rosalind Workbench tool, a harness that aims to help researchers plan experiments and analyze results. The acquisition is a classic example of how the biggest AI labs (namely OpenAI and Anthropic) are building ever more software for the biggest industries, like pharma.

title: Google has joined Amazon in attacking Nvidia’s stronghold with AI app developers
summary: On Tuesday, Google revealed that TorchTPU, its long-awaited version of PyTorch, is now available as an open source project. With this, Google joins Amazon in trying to break Nvidia’s stranglehold on the AI industry, where most AI apps are written by default to run on Nvidia’s chips, or GPUs. PyTorch is the popular open source toolkit that AI app developers and startups use to build, train, and run AI models. Google’s version, TorchTPU, lets AI apps run on Google’s AI chips, called Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). It says it worked directly with Meta, Hugging Face, Inferact (maker of vLLM), RadixArk (maker of SGLang), and others to ensure that TorchTPU’s features and code libraries work well with these popular AI development tools, just as the original PyTorch does. But Amazon and Google are clearly working to end Nvidia’s advantage.

title: ChatGPT now lets you lock your chats
summary: OpenAI revealed on Tuesday that users can now lock ChatGPT conversations to keep sensitive chats private when others may have access to their screen or device. Users can secure their locked chats with a four-digit PIN, or use Face ID or Touch ID on supported devices. The addition of locked chats adds a new layer of privacy to ChatGPT, as the app is increasingly used for personal conversations . OpenAI notes that locking a chat doesn’t create end-to-end encryption or a separate encrypted vault, change how long it retains the chat, remove information that ChatGPT remembered before a chat was locked, or change the “Improve the model for everyone” setting. OpenAI says resetting a PIN permanently deletes all locked chats, files, and other content protected by the previous PIN. Locked Chats will be available to users on ChatGPT Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu plans.

She is the founder and managing partner of Techable Ventures, a VC firm focused on physical AI, which she started after spending nearly seven years as a product marketer at Nvidia. Before that, she held the same role at a company that was later bought by Intel and was a digital signal processing engineer at Interconnect Systems, which was later bought by the electronics manufacturer Molex. She stopped by Equity to talk about the future of physical AI — one of the industry’s latest buzzwords. “A lot of companies and experts have been talking about the ChatGPT moment for robotics,” she said, adding that right now the industry was more in a “LEGO era.” “There are a lot of foundational software and building blocks for robotics that are being rethought right now as we speak, and it’s super important in order for innovation to scale,” she continued.

title: FairStress: A deeper evaluation of fairness in LLM decision-making
summary: Today we’re introducing FairStress , a benchmark for measuring demographic fairness in LLMs beyond the choice a model ultimately makes in decisions impacting people. FairStress is available for download, and we’re also building it into Olmo-eval , our open workbench for running and comparing model evaluations. Across open-weight and frontier models including Olmo, Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Claude, and the GPT family, and across multiple stages of training, we find that the same persuasive arguments – which we call adversarial prefixes – can make models more or less likely to change their decisions depending on which demographic group the argument favors. With FairStress, our target is symmetric fairness —when the evidence supports a decision, a model should apply the same criteria and be equally resistant to changing that decision regardless of which demographic group benefits. FairStress does not attempt to capture every conception of fairness.

title: MPS in PyTorch 2.15
summary: If you run models on your Mac or use MPS as your primary acceleration tool for computing, there's plenty to look forward to in PyTorch 2.15! A quick word about who we are: we're the PyTorch team at Hugging Face. So we run real models from the Hugging Face Hub across language, image and video, find where MPS falls short and fix it upstream in PyTorch, more and more often by replacing MPSGraph with dedicated Metal kernels. PyTorch 2.15 adds torch.float8_e4m3fn tensors on MPS: one byte per value, half the storage of FP16 or BF16. PyTorch 2.16 commits the command buffer every 16 kernels , so the GPU gets to work while the CPU is still encoding the rest. PyTorch 2.15 brings FP8 to the Mac, faster LLM decoding for dense and MoE models, more linear algebra on the GPU and a long list of operations moved from MPSGraph to dedicated Metal kernels.

title: Embedded AI evaluators won’t be an easy solution, Hugging Face’s policy chief says
summary: AI labs have staked their reputations on model benchmarking — the supposedly neutral and accurate system of evaluations that are designed to measure whether one AI product is better than another. However, the methods behind these evaluations are complicated and still maturing, said Irene Solaiman, Hugging Face’s chief policy officer, during a discussion at TechCrunch Disrupt last week. Outside of an individual test’s validity, there’s also the added question of how that test compares to other evaluations. “They are an evolving science — where we don’t know how to meaningfully compare them to each other,” Solaiman said. “They start to get ineffective relatively quickly, and we don’t have as much of a thriving ecosystem as we need,” she added.

title: Microsoft says AI agents are like insider threats as ‘frontier models can’t be trusted’
summary: Microsoft on Monday introduced new security features designed to protect enterprises from the growing threat of AI agents. Project Perception was Microsoft’s answer to powerful hacking models like Anthropic’s Mythos and Fable and OpenAI’s security vulnerability scanning system Daybreak. But lately, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has been warning that the AI enemy may be the very agents enterprises have deployed and are paying for, much like a rogue human employee, otherwise known as an “insider threat.” Earlier this month, in his private blog , Nadella warned that it’s time to stop trusting AI model providers, even if they offer assurances of safety and security with their agentic products. A model provider’s assurances do not relieve us of that responsibility. … In other words, we need to separate the supply of intelligence from the authority over it.” When announcing Guardian Agents, Microsoft’s security business chief Hayete Gallot was even more straightforward.

summary: Tenstorrent, a chip startup focused on inference, has raised $1.5 billion at a $6.2 billion valuation. The round comes five months after the 10-year-old Nvidia challenger reportedly received acquisition interest from Intel and Qualcomm at valuations of as much as $5 billion. The fresh round, which more than doubled Tenstorrent’s valuation from the $2.6 billion it fetched in late 2024, was led by Trace Capital, a new firm launched by Quiet Capital co-founder Ben Mahdavi, and Innovation X. The new capital will go toward scaling chips tailored for serving open-weight AI models and video generation. Tenstorrent is part of a wave of AI hardware startups trying to chip away at Nvidia’s dominance. Among them is Etched, an AI chip maker that was fielding investment offers at valuations of $40 billion or more, TechCrunch reported earlier this month.

title: Making the internet better for AI agents might make it worse for everyone else
summary: But this is being entirely upended by the release of personal AI agents, which can do things for you online, like booking flights or hotel rooms. The mingling of these agents with human visitors—on an internet designed largely to prioritize people—has gone poorly, with many websites blocking AI agents that consumers have sent to negotiate prices or plan vacations. Amazon has blocked Muse’s agents and is waging a court battle against the AI startup Perplexity to block its agents too. Though a judge recently ruled in favor of Perplexity, Amazon has filed an appeal in which it argues that AI agents threaten its advertising business by making it harder to distinguish between ads seen by humans and those served to bots. But that internet might yield to one optimized instead for the agents that will eventually outnumber us, making it even more miserable for the humans who are left.

title: “We were looking at it wrong”: The explosive claim that’s upended the AI world
summary: “I think I have good news about the nature of neural networks.” With those simple words of optimism, Nick Cammarata, a researcher at the AI startup Goodfire, kicked off a 26,000-word blog post that has knocked the AI world on its head, sparking wild speculation as well as cautious (and not-so-cautious) celebration. Cammarata’s claim is that LLMs might in fact be far easier to understand—and thus to monitor and control—than people previously thought. He says he was surprised by the response: “I didn’t expect people to update [their beliefs about AI] quite as much as they did.” “I just really enjoy looking at neural networks,” he says. “Honestly, I really like doing this stuff. And after looking a lot, I have a hopeful story.” It has long been accepted that the mechanisms inside neural networks, the software that underpins most AI models, are very hard—perhaps impossible—to unpick fully. He has built new tools and deploys teams of AI agents to help him make sense of what he sees.

title: People are using AI to make their smart TVs dumb again
summary: With smart TVs in particular, the hacks come at a time when people have grown frustrated with being forced to watch ads and put up with their devices surveilling their viewing habits. If these “dumb TV” hacks become more popular among everyday consumers, they have the potential to disrupt the smart TV ad industry, which profits from selling viewing data to advertisers or using it to display personalized ads on their own interfaces. To use this hack, the developer, Muzzammil Yasin Sabuwala, suggests pointing your preferred AI agent at the dumbtv repository on GitHub. Others warned that AI agents could make mistakes, possibly disabling important packages or breaking things in the process. One person even said they bricked their Android TV using Claude , and another got stuck halfway through hacking their Fire TV.

title: WhatsApp Help Pages Leaked Hidden Instructions for a Meta Chatbot
summary: Dozens of WhatsApp web pages designed to answer people’s questions about Meta’s encrypted messaging app inadvertently exposed the company’s own instructions to its chatbot. A new analysis has found that around 80 help and FAQ pages across WhatsApp’s website exposed text instructions that were designed for a large language model, specifically one of Meta’s own. The instructions, based on findings from privacy company Redact, appeared in the webpages’ code and contained written details that were not explicitly on the WhatsApp help pages. Among the 100 blocks of hidden text, the directions appeared to provide guidance to steer an LLM from answering users questions in unhelpful ways and provide a glimpse at how instructions for chatbots are created. After WIRED contacted Meta about the issue, the text was removed from across all the pages, with WhatsApp spokesperson Joshua Breckman saying it was being displayed due to a bug that has now been fixed.

title: Nvidia launches new open models to run agents in the enterprise and on PCs
summary: Nvidia on Thursday launched new open-weight models designed for always-on agents and edge computing. Such PCs, aimed at consumers, programmers, and enterprise knowledge workers, are being released right now into the market through partners like Microsoft and Dell. “Any organization that wants to run agents on Nvidia infrastructure now has an open, optimized model for their tier without having to choose between capability and deployability,” Nvidia’s vice president of Open Models and Software, Kari Briski, wrote in the blog post announcing these models. Nvidia claims that the Super VL completes tasks faster than competing models from Anthropic and OpenAI (Opus 5, GPT 6.1 Sol, Luna, Astra) when post-trained on specific agentic tasks. Of course, these aren’t the first open-weight models that Nvidia has released that compete with the proprietary frontier labs — companies that are both its customers and its investments.

title: A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents
summary: The AI agents carried out the attacks with little involvement from the human hacker. The AI agents carried out the attacks with little involvement from the human hacker. A hacker broke into more than 100 websites using an army of AI agents that mostly operated on their own, based on findings from the AI security firm Norforge . Though Norforge doesn’t name the targets, Reuters reports that the victims included companies like John Deere, SharkNinja, and Cummins. However, as noted by Norforge, hackers can also use the tool to orchestrate cyberattacks using AI agents. John Deere and SharkNinja didn’t immediately respond to The Verge ’s request for comment.

title: Karnataka’s ElevenLabs Partnership Irks Indian Voice AI Startups
summary: India’s AI startups are building homegrown alternatives to global products, yet state governments have been eyeing partnerships with foreign players, making it harder for them to find customers at home. ElevenLabs recently signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS) to explore using voice AI in Kannada across citizen services, skilling, and grievance redressal. But the Karnataka government’s decision to partner with a US-based startup for government services hasn’t resonated well with Indian startups. Earlier this year, it also formed joint working groups with Anthropic to explore AI skilling across the state through Claude certifications. “When government services rely on foreign AI platforms, we’re potentially exposing sensitive conversations between Indian citizens and their government to entities operating under foreign jurisdictions,” Dheemanth Reddy, Co-founder and CEO of voice AI startup Maya Research , tells AIM.

title: Can Zero Egress Give Cloudflare an Edge in Data Platform Market?
summary: Cloud data warehouses charge massive exit fees for egress, ie moving data across platforms, and these bills stack up when querying or federating data. Cloudflare recently launched a serverless data platform called Basin, built on Apache Iceberg and the company’s R2 object storage, which gives teams an open way to ingest, store, catalogue, and query analytical data across the tools they already use. With Basin, Cloudflare pitches for a standard setup in the age of demanding analytics, provisioning servers ahead of demand, wiring together separate tools for collection, storage, and querying, and paying to move data between clouds. Besides, ingestion, catalogue management, and querying are all serverless on Cloudflare's network, meaning no sizing, no separate systems to stitch, and no egress fees to access the data elsewhere. “Basin’s architecture is what allows it to be economical,” Meagan Gamache, Director of Product Management of Developer Platforms at Cloudflare, tells AIM.

title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
summary: Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone . The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox. The researchers say Eko’s behavior has what classic studies, including work by the influential University of Tennessee psychologist Gordon Burghardt, suggest are four hallmarks associated with play in humans and animals: The agents invented their own rules and challenges, repeated activities with slight variations, pretended objects were other objects, and pursued goals just for the sake of it. Eko then decided that the catches had happened too quickly to really count, so it canceled its record and started again with stricter rules. “This is playing,” says Norelli.

title: Disney Asked Character.AI to Go Bankrupt for a Get-Out-of-Lawsuits Card
summary: While some saw the fall of a chatbot platform as a harbinger for the industry , court filings indicate that the decision was actually a key part of a deal that has let Disney hire most of Character.AI’s staff—including its now former CEO Karandeep Anand —potentially acquire most of Character.AI’s technology , and avoid the beleaguered startup’s many legal liabilities and obligations. In the past few years, Character.AI has faced multiple private lawsuits over the safety of its chatbots, as well as investigations from regulators around the world. In the case of Character.AI, a motion filed by Character.AI’s legal counsel says that Disney required that the deal be “fully consummated” through bankruptcy proceedings because of the startup’s “diminishing cash reserve and significant litigation and regulatory risks.” A spokesperson for Character.AI referred WIRED to Disney for comment on whether the deal was contingent on the startup declaring bankruptcy.

title: Claude Code is 3x Faster, Thanks to a 34 Year Old Tool
summary: Anthropic has improved the latency of Claude Code across multiple platforms. Compared to August, it is now 3x faster on local sessions, 2.8x faster on cloud sessions, and 1.5x faster on API, chat, and Cowork platforms. The company used gzip, a data compression utility released in 1992, to improve performance. “Claude Code now gzips the conversation it sends on every turn, so it reaches the model faster,” said Anthropic in a post on X. “Cloud sessions also start up as soon as you start typing.” These improvements are measured at the 90th percentile (p90) for the wait before the first token, excluding model processing time—meaning it likely isolates delays from factors such as conversation transmission and session startup. These improvements follow last month’s 3x performance boost for Claude on desktop and web Anthropic said a two-week engineering sprint merged more than 3,000 changes to speed up Claude’s web and desktop interfaces.

title: AI Agent Breach Exposes Flaws in India’s Autonomous System Defences
summary: Rogue AI agents have reached India’s shores. Last week, the Computer Emergency Response Team - India (CERT-In) disclosed that several Indian organisations were targeted by AI agents being tested by frontier AI companies. India is only the latest country to report AI agents hacking a live system. The incidents have renewed concerns about what happens when AI agents, designed to execute multi-step tasks with limited human intervention, interact with sensitive systems such as government portals and financial institutions. The company’s 2026 Voice of the CISO report also found that 42% of Indian security leaders identified AI assistants, copilots , and autonomous agents as a top concern. Singh argues that permission-based security alone would not be sufficient as AI agents become more autonomous.

title: Anthropic to Set Aside 5% Stock for New Public Benefit Fund
summary: Anthropic plans to commit 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund, as the AI company seeks to direct a portion of its growth towards addressing the broader societal impact of artificial intelligence. The proposed Anthropic Public Benefit Fund could support large donations to nonprofits and direct distributions to specific populations. The commitment is subject to stockholder approval, with the company also considering additional equity contributions as its valuation rises. “AI may generate enormous economic value, but it could also cause instability for many workers,” Anthropic wrote . The move comes as Anthropic prepares for a potential public listing and faces growing questions about how the economic gains from AI should be shared. The fund’s stake could increase as Anthropic grows.

title: Utho Cloud Opens B300 GPU Bookings Ahead of February 2027 Rollout
summary: Indian cloud provider Utho Cloud has opened reservations for NVIDIA B300 GPUs in India ahead of a planned February 2027 deployment, offering AI companies and enterprises committed computing capacity with rupee-based billing and India-hosted infrastructure. The company said that organisations can reserve GPU capacity for one, two, or three years. The NVIDIA B300, based on the Blackwell Ultra architecture, comes with 288GB of HBM3e memory and supports workloads such as large language model training, inference, and AI agents. GPU availability, infrastructure costs, and data residency requirements remain considerations for businesses planning to train and deploy AI models. Utho has outlined plans to invest in and deploy 10,000 GPUs, but it did not provide further details on the deployment timeline or the number of B300 GPUs available for reservation. Utho Cloud serves more than 51,000 customers, including over 3,500 B2B clients.

title: Birla AI Labs Launches Yug-1, a Time Series Foundation Model Built in India
summary: Birla AI Labs, an AI initiative and venture studio under the Aditya Birla Group, has released Yug-1, its first time series foundation model (TSFM), developed to forecast outcomes, identify patterns, and detect anomalies across interconnected datasets. TSFMs are large-scale AI models pre-trained on a diverse collection of universal temporal patterns, such as weather, traffic, finance, retail, and energy records. Ananya Birla, Founder and Chairperson of Birla AI Labs, said Yug-1 outperformed other first-generation TSMFs on the GiftEval benchmark and performed competitively against newer-generation models. Time series models are used in applications such as demand forecasting, financial analysis, equipment monitoring, and infrastructure planning. Birla AI Labs described Yug-1 as Asia’s first TSMF built for real-world use. Birla also encouraged developers to test the model and provide feedback, which she said would help shape its future development.

title: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings
summary: The composition of Anthropic’s workforce and the type of work getting done have changed significantly in the past year, based on a report that the AI company published on Friday. Anthropic argues that its own workplace trends could be indicators of “how AI will shift work organization, hiring, and labor demand across the economy,” especially since the company “has thoroughly molded its workflows around AI.” But even if other organizations never embrace AI as thoroughly or in the exact same way as Anthropic, the report offers an intriguing glimpse at how the company currently operates. Notably, Anthropic is making fewer junior hires, with the proportion of junior-level employees in technical departments falling from 21% to 14% since early 2025, and the proportion of junior technical hires falling even more sharply, from 27% to 9%.

title: Replit makes OpenAI its default over Anthropic, CEO says
summary: Replit revealed a partnership with OpenAI in August, but there was never any indication that it was no longer partnering with Anthropic. “I think ChatGPT is better now,” Masad said, adding that the company uses an internal benchmark to help assess metrics like performance. “We publish a public benchmark as well, and consistently, Sol and Astra perform better on building vibe-coded applications from scratch. After Disrupt, Masad clarified that customers can still access Anthropic models on the platform, but that OpenAI’s ChatGPT is now the default. This shift could significantly reduce Replit’s spend with Anthropic since most customers stick with the default rather than selecting a model themselves. Prior to striking a deal with OpenAI, Replit relied on Anthropic’s Claude models to run its platform. That partnership was said to have helped the company grow its revenue significantly, and Masad noted on stage that Replit had been, until recently, a top-five customer of Anthropic’s.

title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
summary: OpenAI, Meta, and Google want AI agents to do everything for you. OpenAI, Meta, and Google want AI agents to do everything for you. In recent weeks, users of services like Meta’s Muse, xAI’s Grok, OpenAI’s Dots, and Instinct have reported blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks across top websites. Amazon was already fighting off AI agents last year when it banned Perplexity’s agentic shopping feature and sued the AI startup , raising legal and practical questions about the future of agents on the web. Even if websites aren’t banning AI agents outright, agents may still be clashing with anti-bot systems This ongoing legal battle didn’t stop OpenAI, Meta, and Google from rolling out agents of their own.
